notes.meaning: David cries out to the Lord three times, begging God to listen closely to his honest plea. He comes to God with a clean conscience, speaking without lies or deceit. Insincere prayers bear no fruit, but God listens when people bring their honest needs before Him.

David asks God to act as his judge and declare him innocent. He knows that human courts can be unfair, but God's courtroom is completely just. He leaves the verdict in God's hands instead of trying to take revenge himself.

God examined David in the quiet of the night, when a person's deepest thoughts come out. Like gold tested in a hot furnace to remove impurities, David was proven to have pure motives without an evil plot. He made up his mind not to let wicked words pass his lips.

David watched how violent people lived in the world around him. Instead of following their cruel example, he let God's spoken word guide his steps and keep him safe from harm. God's truth protects believers from falling into destructive ways.

David kept his walk closely aligned with God's commands and stayed on the right path. Even while walking faithfully, he knew he needed the Lord's strength so his feet would not slip. God gives the grace people need to stay on track.

David turns to prayer with strong confidence because he knows God will answer him. He asks God to bend down His ear and hear his words. True faith keeps praying because it rests on God's willingness to listen.

David asks God to display His wonderful covenant love, which is God's loyal and unfailing devotion to His people. God's right hand stands for His mighty power, which He uses to protect those who run to Him for safety. He rescues all who trust Him when enemies attack.

David uses two vivid pictures to ask for God's protection. The apple of the eye means the pupil, which is tender and guarded with great care. The shadow of God's wings pictures a mother bird sheltering her helpless chicks from danger.

Cruel attackers closed in on David from every side to destroy him. These enemies were after his very life and would not stop until he was dead. In the middle of deadly peril, he turned to God as his only shelter.

David's enemies grew fat and prosperous, which made them unfeeling and hard-hearted toward others. Their wealth filled them with pride, and they boasted loudly against God and His people. When people trust in money, their hearts often turn cold.

The hunters tracked David down and trapped him wherever he turned. They locked their eyes on him, waiting for the right moment to throw him to the ground. God's servants often feel cornered by trouble, but God still sees their steps.

David compares his enemy to a hungry lion that is eager to tear its prey to pieces. Like a fierce young lion crouching in secret, the attacker was waiting in ambush to pounce. This shows the cruel and sneaky nature of those who oppose God's people.

David calls on the Lord to rise up like a champion and confront the attacker head-on. He prays that God will bring the enemy down to his knees before he can strike. God's mighty sword of justice is what rescues His people from evil hands.

David asks for rescue from people whose only goal is earthly reward in this short life. They live only for worldly wealth and pass their leftovers to their children. In contrast, God cares for His treasured people and provides them with blessings that truly satisfy.

David knows his true reward is not earthly wealth, but seeing God's face in righteousness. When he awakes, beholding God's glorious presence will bring complete and lasting satisfaction to his soul. Believers find their greatest joy in being close to God rather than having the things of this world.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars view waking up as rising each morning to God's renewed favor after a night of prayer, or waking to relief after a season of dark trouble, rather than waking from death in the resurrection.
